subject: BPSC CS Numericals & Output Tracing Drill
exam_relevance: 15-20 numerical/output questions expected in BPSC TRE CS

questions.question: What is the decimal equivalent of the binary number (1011.1101)₂?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.question: Which of the following correctly equals the decimal number 53?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.question: What is the octal equivalent of the binary number (110101110)₂?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Group in 3 bits from right: 110 101 110 → 6 5 6. Thus (110101110)₂ = (656)₈.

questions.question: Convert the binary number (101111101010)₂ into hexadecimal.

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.question: What is the decimal value of the hexadecimal number (2F)₁₆?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.question: Which of the following correctly represents the decimal number 255 in another number base?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.question: What is the 4-bit Gray code equivalent of the binary number (1011)₂?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: MSB stays 1; then 1⊕0=1, 0⊕1=1, 1⊕1=0. Gray code = 1110.

questions.question: Convert the 4-bit Gray code (1101) into standard binary.

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.question: What is the 8421 BCD representation of the decimal number 79?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Encode each decimal digit separately in 4-bit binary: 7 → 0111, 9 → 1001. BCD = 0111 1001.

questions.question: What is the representable integer range for an 8-bit signed number in 2's complement form?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: An n-bit 2's complement number spans -(2^(n-1)) to +(2^(n-1)-1). For n=8, range is -128 to +127.

questions.question: What decimal value does the 8-bit 2's complement binary number 11110110 represent?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: MSB is 1 (negative). Invert bits: 00001001, add 1 → 00001010 = 10. Value = -10.

questions.question: What is the 2's complement of the 8-bit binary number 00101100?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: 1's complement of 00101100 is 11010011. Adding 1 yields 11010100, which is none of A, B, C.

questions.question: Convert the fractional binary number (1101.101)₂ to decimal.

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.question: Convert the decimal fraction (0.6875)₁₀ into binary.

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.question: Which of the following correctly represents the decimal number (60)₁₀?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.question: A microprocessor with a 16-bit address bus can directly address a maximum memory of:

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: 2¹⁶ = 65,536 memory locations = 64 KB (assuming byte-addressable memory).

questions.question: What is the maximum byte-addressable memory supported by a 20-bit address bus (as in 8086)?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.question: How much byte-addressable physical memory can a CPU with a 24-bit address bus access?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.question: A 32-bit address bus can address a maximum byte-addressable memory space of:

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: 2³² = 2² × 2³⁰ = 4 × 1 GB = 4 GB.

questions.question: Which 8086 Segment:Offset pairs produce the 20-bit physical address 21234H?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.question: In 8086, if SS = 3450H and SP = 0120H, what is the calculated 20-bit physical stack address?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.question: A cache has a hit time of 2 ns, main memory access time of 50 ns, and hit ratio of 0.90. Using T_avg = h×T_c + (1-h)×(T_c+T_m), what is EMAT?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.question: A cache hit time is 5 ns and miss penalty (additional time on miss) is 95 ns. If hit ratio is 95%, what is the average memory access time?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: AMAT = Hit time + (1 - Hit rate) × Miss penalty = 5 + 0.05 × 95 = 5 + 4.75 = 9.75 ns.

questions.question: Out of 1000 memory references, 850 are found in cache. What is the cache hit ratio and miss ratio?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.question: A non-pipelined CPU takes 50 ns per instruction. A 5-stage pipeline has a 10 ns clock cycle. What is the ideal speedup for large n?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Ideal speedup = T_nonpipe / T_stage = 50 ns / 10 ns = 5 times. None of 4, 8, or 10 is 5.

questions.question: How many clock cycles are needed to execute 100 instructions in an ideal 4-stage instruction pipeline?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: A k-stage pipeline takes k + (n - 1) cycles for n instructions: 4 + (100 - 1) = 103 cycles.

questions.question: How many 1 KB × 8 RAM chips are required to construct a 16 KB × 8 memory system?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Number of chips = (16 KB × 8) / (1 KB × 8) = 16 chips.

questions.question: How many 4K × 4 RAM chips are needed to build a 16K × 8 memory module?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.question: Which of the following memory-to-address-line relationships is CORRECT?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: 2¹⁶=64 KB, 2²⁰=1 MB, and 2³²=4 GB. All three statements A, B, and C are mathematically exact.

questions.question: If a main memory of 64 MB is divided into cache blocks of 64 bytes each, how many blocks exist in main memory?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: 64 MB = 2²⁶ bytes; block size = 64 bytes = 2⁶ bytes. Number of blocks = 2²⁶ / 2⁶ = 2²⁰ blocks.

questions.question: If the page size in a paging system is 4 KB, how many bits are needed for the page offset?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: 4 KB = 4 × 1024 = 4096 = 2¹² bytes. Therefore, 12 bits are required for the page offset.

questions.question: In a 32-bit virtual address space with a page size of 4 KB, how many bits represent the virtual page number (VPN)?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Offset = 12 bits (4 KB = 2¹²). Remaining VPN bits = 32 - 12 = 20 bits.

questions.question: A process has a 64 KB logical address space and a page size of 2 KB. How many entries are in its page table?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Number of pages = 64 KB / 2 KB = 32 pages, so the page table contains 32 entries.

questions.question: A system has 32-bit virtual addresses, 4 KB pages, and each page table entry is 4 bytes. What is the single-level page table size per process?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Pages = 2³² / 2¹² = 2²⁰. Table size = 2²⁰ × 4 bytes = 4 MB.

questions.question: A process of size 10 MB is swapped out at a disk transfer rate of 20 MB/s with 0 ms latency. What is the swap-out time?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Transfer time = Data size / Transfer rate = 10 MB / (20 MB/s) = 0.50 seconds (500 ms).

questions.question: Four processes P1, P2, P3, P4 arrive at t=0 with burst times 6, 8, 7, 3 ms. Using FCFS scheduling, what is the average waiting time?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.question: For processes arriving at t=0 with burst times 6, 8, 7, 3 ms, what is the average waiting time under non-preemptive SJF?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: SJF order: 3, 6, 7, 8. Waiting times: 0, 3, 9, 16. Average = (0+3+9+16)/4 = 28/4 = 7.00 ms.

questions.question: Three processes arrive at t=0 with burst times 4, 2, 6 ms. Under Round Robin with time quantum q = 2 ms, what is the average waiting time?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Completion times: P2=4, P1=8, P3=12. Waiting times: P1=8-4=4, P2=4-2=2, P3=12-6=6. Avg = (4+2+6)/3 = 4.0 ms.

questions.question: If 3 processes arrive at t=0 with bursts 10, 5, 8 ms under FCFS, what is the average turnaround time?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Completion times: P1=10, P2=15, P3=23. Turnaround avg = (10+15+23)/3 = 48/3 = 16.0 ms.

questions.question: A disk queue has requests at tracks 98, 183, 37, 122, 14 with initial head at track 53. Using FCFS, what is total head movement?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.question: For disk requests 98, 183, 37, 122, 14 with initial head at 53, what is total head movement using SSTF?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.question: Given page reference string 1, 2, 3, 4, 1, 2, 5, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 3 frames, how many page faults occur under FIFO?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: FIFO faults occur on: 1,2,3,4,1,2,5,3,4 (last 1,2,5 hit) → total = 9 page faults.

questions.question: Given page reference string 7, 0, 1, 2, 0, 3, 0, 4, 2, 3 with 3 frames, how many page faults occur under LRU?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Faults at 7, 0, 1, 2, (0 hit), 3, (0 hit), 4, 2, 3 → 8 page faults in LRU (vs 9 in FIFO).

questions.question: If TLB hit ratio is 80%, TLB access takes 10 ns, and main memory access takes 100 ns (single-level page table), what is effective memory access time?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.question: In a system with 5 identical units of resource R shared by 4 processes, each needing at most 2 units of R, is deadlock possible?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Safe minimum = n×(k-1)+1 = 4×(2-1)+1 = 5. With 5 units, at least one process can get 2 units and finish; deadlock is impossible.

questions.question: How many resources of type R are needed to guarantee NO deadlock among 4 processes if each process needs at most 3 units?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Minimum deadlock-free units = n×(k - 1) + 1 = 4×(3 - 1) + 1 = 8 + 1 = 9 units.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about page size and page offset bits is TRUE?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: 2¹⁰ = 1 KB, 2¹³ = 8 KB, and 2¹⁴ = 16 KB. All three statements A, B, and C are correct.

questions.question: If a semaphore S is initialized to 5, and 3 wait(P) and 2 signal(V) operations are executed, what is the final value of S?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: S = 5 - 3 (wait decrements) + 2 (signal increments) = 4.

questions.question: If a physical memory is 256 MB and frame size is 4 KB, how many physical frames exist?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: 256 MB = 2²⁸ bytes; frame size = 4 KB = 2¹² bytes. Frames = 2²⁸ / 2¹² = 2¹⁶ (65,536) frames.

questions.question: Which of the following is true for FIFO page replacement with 4 frames on string 1,2,3,4,1,2,5,1,2,3,4,5?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: With 4 frames FIFO causes 10 faults vs 9 faults with 3 frames — a classic example of Belady's anomaly. All A, B, C hold.

questions.question: What is the postfix form of the infix expression A + B * (C - D)?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Parentheses first: (C-D) → CD-; then B*(C-D) → BCD-*; then A+... → ABCD-*+.

questions.question: Convert the infix expression (A + B) * (C - D) / E into postfix form.

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: AB+ and CD- multiply to AB+CD-*, then divide by E (same precedence, left-to-right) → AB+CD-*E/.

questions.question: Evaluate the postfix expression: 5 3 2 * + 4 -

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.question: What is the evaluated value of the postfix expression: 6 2 / 3 + 4 * ?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.question: What is the maximum number of nodes in a binary tree of height h (where root has height 0)?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Levels 0 through h have 1 + 2 + 4 + ... + 2^h = 2^(h+1) - 1 maximum nodes.

questions.question: Which of the following holds true for a full binary tree that has 15 total nodes?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: For 15 nodes: leaves L = (15+1)/2 = 8, internal nodes = 7, edges = 15-1 = 14. All A, B, C hold.

questions.question: If the preorder traversal of a Binary Search Tree (BST) is 30, 20, 10, 25, 40, 35, 50, what is its postorder traversal?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Root=30, Left={20,10,25}→postorder 10,25,20; Right={40,35,50}→postorder 35,50,40; then root 30.

questions.question: A 2D array A[10][20] of 4-byte integers starts at base address 1000 (0-indexed). What is the address of A[2][5] in Row-Major order?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.question: For A[10][20] (4-byte elements, base 1000, 0-indexed), what is the address of A[2][5] in Column-Major order?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.question: What is the value of the permutation 6P3?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.question: What is the value of the combination 8C3?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.question: By the Pigeonhole Principle, what is the minimum number of students needed to guarantee at least 3 were born in the same month?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Worst case: 2 per month across 12 months = 24. Adding 1 more guarantees 3 in some month: 24 + 1 = 25.

questions.question: How many edges does a complete undirected graph K7 with 7 vertices have?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Edges in Kn = n(n - 1)/2 = 7 × 6 / 2 = 21 edges.

questions.question: If a connected planar graph has 6 vertices and 10 edges, how many faces (regions) does it have by Euler's formula?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Euler's formula: V - E + F = 2 → 6 - 10 + F = 2 → F = 6 faces.

questions.question: How many edges are present in any spanning tree of a connected graph with 12 vertices and 30 edges?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Any tree (including a spanning tree) with n vertices has exactly n - 1 edges: 12 - 1 = 11 edges.

questions.question: Which of the following formulas equals 10C4?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: 10C4 = (10×9×8×7)/24 = 210, which also equals 10C6 (symmetry) and 10P4/4!. All three A, B, C are correct.

questions.question: What is the maximum height (edges from root to deepest leaf) of a binary search tree with 7 nodes?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: A skewed binary tree with n=7 nodes has height n - 1 = 6 edges. None of 2, 3, or 7 is 6.

questions.question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does Binary Search need on a sorted array of 1024 items?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Worst-case comparisons in binary search = ⌊log₂ n⌋ + 1 = 10 + 1 = 11 comparisons.

questions.question: A graph has 5 vertices with degrees 4, 3, 3, 2, 2. How many edges does the graph have?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: By Handshaking Lemma: 2E = sum of degrees = 4+3+3+2+2 = 14 → E = 7 edges.

questions.question: Evaluate the postfix expression: 2 3 ^ 4 + 5 -

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.question: How many usable host IP addresses are available in an IPv4 /24 subnet?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Host bits = 32 - 24 = 8. Usable hosts = 2⁸ - 2 = 256 - 2 = 254 (subtracting network and broadcast).

questions.question: How many usable host addresses are available in a /25 IPv4 subnet?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Host bits = 32 - 25 = 7. Usable hosts = 2⁷ - 2 = 128 - 2 = 126.

questions.question: How many usable host addresses exist in a /26 IPv4 subnet?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Host bits = 32 - 26 = 6. Usable hosts = 2⁶ - 2 = 64 - 2 = 62.

questions.question: How many usable host IP addresses does a /28 IPv4 subnet provide?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Host bits = 32 - 28 = 4. Usable hosts = 2⁴ - 2 = 16 - 2 = 14.

questions.question: A /30 IPv4 subnet (commonly used for point-to-point router links) yields how many usable host addresses?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Host bits = 32 - 30 = 2. Usable hosts = 2² - 2 = 4 - 2 = 2.

questions.question: If a Class C network 192.168.1.0/24 is subnetted with mask 255.255.255.224, how many subnets and usable hosts per subnet are created?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: 224 = 11100000₂ (3 borrowed bits → 2³ = 8 subnets; 5 host bits → 2⁵ - 2 = 30 usable hosts).

questions.question: Which of the following correctly expresses the size of an IPv6 address?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: An IPv6 address is 128 bits = 16 bytes (128/8) = 32 hexadecimal digits (128/4). All three are equivalent.

questions.question: In a 10-node full mesh network topology, how many dedicated point-to-point links are required?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Links = N(N - 1)/2 = 10 × 9 / 2 = 45 dedicated links.

questions.question: What is the output of the C++ snippet (assuming 4-byte int): int x = 5; cout << sizeof(x++) << " " << x;

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: sizeof() is evaluated at compile time and NEVER evaluates its operand expression! So x stays 5.

questions.question: What is the output of the C++ code: int a = 10; int b = a++; cout << a << " " << b;

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Post-increment (a++) assigns the old value 10 to b first, then increments a to 11. Output: 11 10.

questions.question: What is the output of: int a = 10; int b = ++a; cout << a << " " << b;

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Pre-increment (++a) increments a to 11 first, then assigns 11 to b. Output: 11 11.

questions.question: How many times does the loop body execute: for(int i = 0; i < 10; i += 2) { cout << i; }

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: i takes values 0, 2, 4, 6, 8 (stops when i=10). Thus the body executes 5 times.

questions.question: What is the output of: int arr[] = {10, 20, 30, 40}; int *p = arr + 1; cout << *(p + 2);

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: p points to arr[1] (20). p + 2 points to arr[3], whose value is 40.

questions.question: What is the output of: int x = 15, y = 4; cout << (x / y) << " " << (x % y);

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Integer division 15 / 4 truncates to 3, and modulo 15 % 4 gives remainder 3. Output: 3 3.

questions.question: What is the output of: int i = 0; while(i++ < 3) cout << i;

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Checks 0<3 (i becomes 1, prints 1), 1<3 (prints 2), 2<3 (prints 3), 3<3 false (i becomes 4). Output: 123.

questions.question: What is the output of the C++ snippet: int a = 5, b = 3; cout << (a & b) << " " << (a | b);

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: 5=0101₂, 3=0011₂. Bitwise AND = 0001₂ = 1; Bitwise OR = 0111₂ = 7. Output: 1 7.

questions.question: What does the C++ code print: char s[] = "BPSC"; cout << sizeof(s) << " " << strlen(s);

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: sizeof(s) counts the null terminator '\0' (5 bytes), while strlen(s) counts characters before '\0' (4).

questions.question: What is the output of: int x = 1; switch(x) { case 1: cout << "A"; case 2: cout << "B"; break; default: cout << "C"; }

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Without a break after case 1, execution falls through into case 2, printing AB and then breaking.

questions.question: What is the output of recursive call f(4) for: int f(int n){ return (n <= 1) ? 1 : n * f(n - 2); }

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.question: What is the output of: int x = 3; cout << (x << 2);

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Left-shifting 3 (0011₂) by 2 bits multiplies by 2² = 4: 3 × 4 = 12 (1100₂).

questions.question: What is the output of the SQL query: SELECT ROUND(15.678, 1);

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: ROUND(15.678, 1) rounds to 1 decimal place; since the 2nd decimal digit is 7 (>=5), it rounds up to 15.7.

questions.question: What is the output of the SQL query: SELECT MOD(29, 5);

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: MOD(29, 5) returns the remainder of 29 divided by 5: 29 = 5×5 + 4, so output is 4.

questions.question: What does the SQL query SELECT LENGTH('BPSC_TRE'); return?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The string 'BPSC_TRE' has 8 characters (B, P, S, C, _, T, R, E), so LENGTH returns 8.

questions.question: In standard SQL (1-based indexing), what does SELECT SUBSTR('COMPUTER', 4, 3); return?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Starting at 1-based position 4 ('P'), extracting 3 characters yields 'PUT'.

questions.question: Table T has 5 rows with column Marks = {10, NULL, 20, NULL, 30}. What do COUNT(*) and COUNT(Marks) return?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: COUNT(*) counts all rows including NULLs (5), whereas COUNT(column) ignores NULL values (3).

questions.question: For Marks = {10, NULL, 20, 30}, what does SELECT AVG(Marks) return in SQL?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: SQL aggregate AVG ignores NULLs: sum = 10 + 20 + 30 = 60, count of non-NULLs = 3, AVG = 60/3 = 20.

questions.question: What does SELECT ROUND(145.67, -1); return in SQL?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: A negative second argument (-1) rounds to the nearest ten: 145.67 rounds up to 150.

questions.question: Which of the following SQL queries returns the integer 5?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: INSTR('DATABASE','BASE')=5 (1-based), LENGTH('MYSQL')=5, and MOD(23,6)=5. All three return 5.

questions.question: If relation R has 4 rows and relation S has 5 rows, how many rows are in the Cartesian product R CROSS JOIN S?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: A CROSS JOIN (Cartesian product) produces |R| × |S| = 4 × 5 = 20 rows.

questions.question: Which of the following SQL/C++ statements produces the value 16?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: POWER(2,4)=16, (2<<3)=2×8=16, and LENGTH('BPSC')*4 = 4×4 = 16. All three A, B, and C output 16.
